summary: Nearly every visitor needs a visa for Afghanistan, issued through Afghan embassies and consulates operating under the Taliban administration. A visa on arrival at Kabul airport is issued only against an official letter or invitation, and foreign nationals of Afghan origin can enter on an entry permit without a visa. Nearly every government advises against all travel: armed attacks, kidnapping and arbitrary detention are serious risks, and consular help inside the country is effectively unavailable.

notes: Alcohol is strictly prohibited — do not bring any into the country, including duty-free.
Drones are banned for visitors, and satellite phones or professional camera equipment can attract suspicion and detention. Leave them at home.

payments.text: Afghanistan is a cash economy. Cards are useless outside a handful of Kabul hotels, the banking system barely functions for foreigners, and US dollars are widely exchanged at money markets. Carry cash discreetly and in stages.

safety.text: The UK government advises against all travel to Afghanistan, even with an organised tour group. The security situation is volatile, there is a high risk of foreigners being detained or kidnapped, terrorists often target places frequented by foreign nationals, and in-person consular help is not possible.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring (April–May) and fall (September–October) avoid the harsh mountain winters and intense summer heat — though safety, not weather, should dominate any decision to travel.

tips.text: The US, UK, EU states, Canada and Australia all advise against ALL travel to Afghanistan. Foreigners have been detained for months without charge. If you go regardless, use specialist security support, share your itinerary with your embassy, and understand that rescue options are minimal.

The Taliban impose severe restrictions on women: mandatory hijab, mahram (male guardian) expectations for many activities, and exclusion from many public spaces. Women travelers report being refused service when unaccompanied and face particular scrutiny — weigh this honestly before traveling.

Checkpoints are frequent and run by different authorities. Some provinces require permission letters for foreigners, and photographing officials, checkpoints or government buildings can lead to detention — always ask before pointing a camera.

There is no eVisa. Tourists apply in person at an Afghan embassy in a third country. The missions in Dubai, Islamabad, Peshawar and Doha issue tourist visas under the current administration; requirements differ by mission, so contact them directly first. A visa on arrival at Kabul International Airport exists only for visitors with an official letter from an Afghan organisation or an invitation from an international organisation working in Afghanistan, approved by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Sharia law as interpreted by the Taliban applies to everyone: alcohol is banned, dress codes apply to men as well as women, and behavior that is unremarkable elsewhere (music in public, mixed-gender socialising) can cause serious trouble.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Afghanistan?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you are a foreign national of Afghan origin: if your passport gives Afghanistan as your place of birth, or you hold a tazkira, an Afghan passport or a certificate of identity from an Afghan mission, you can enter on an entry permit without a visa. Everyone else needs a visa, and there is no eVisa. Tourists apply in person at an Afghan embassy or consulate; the missions in Dubai, Islamabad, Peshawar and Doha handle most tourist applications under the current administration. A visa on arrival at Kabul International Airport is issued only against an official letter from an Afghan organisation or an invitation from an international organisation working in Afghanistan, with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' approval.

faq.question: Is Afghanistan safe to visit?
faq.answer: No. Nearly every government advises against all travel to Afghanistan, citing terrorism, kidnapping and arbitrary detention of foreigners. Several foreign visitors have been detained for extended periods since 2021, and no country can provide effective consular help inside Afghanistan.

faq.question: Can women travel to Afghanistan?
faq.answer: Entry is legally possible with a visa, but the Taliban's restrictions on women are severe — mandatory dress rules, male-guardian expectations and exclusion from many public places. Solo women travelers report being refused hotels and services. Most governments specifically warn women against traveling.

faq.question: Are visas issued by Afghan embassies valid at the border?
faq.answer: Yes. Visas issued by Afghan missions now operating under Taliban administration are accepted at Kabul airport and land borders the authorities control. Get up-to-date guidance from the mission that issues your visa, as procedures change without notice.

faq.question: Can I use cards or ATMs in Afghanistan?
faq.answer: Realistically, no. Bring all the money you need in cash — US dollars exchange readily into afghani at money markets. Keep it split and discreet, and confirm the current rules on how much cash you may bring in and take out.
